newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Pakistan awards oil products tender for 1Q 1997.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan awards oil products tender for 1Q 1997.

text.p: Pakistan's Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Resources has awarded a total of 480,000 tonnes of of diesel in eight cargoes in its tender for first quarter 1997 deliveries, a ministry official said on Thursday.
Five 60,000-tonne cargoes of 1.0-percent sulphur diesel were awarded to Swiss trader Glencore.
Three cargoes--one cargo to be delivered each month between January and March--were awarded at a premium of $1.10 per barrel to MidEast spot quotes on a cost-and-freight (c-and-f) basis to Keamari.
The remaining two cargoes will be delivered on an optional basis in January and March and was awarded at a premium of $1.34 per barrel to MidEast spot quotes, c-and-f Keamari.
Three cargoes were awarded to MidEast trader Bakri Trading, at a $1.34-per-barrel premium to MidEast spot quotes, c-and-f Keamari.
One cargo is for delivery in January and one in March. The remaining cargo for delivery in February was on an optional basis.

Pakistan also bought two 25,000-tonne cargoes of 80-octane leaded gasoline from Pakistani trader Hascombe at a $16.475-per-tonne-premium to MidEast naphtha quotes, c-and-f Keamari. The cargoes are for February and March deliveries each.
Pakistan purchased all its fuel oil cargoes from Bakri Trading.
It bought two 50,000-tonne cargoes of 125-centistoke, 3.5-percent sulphur fuel oil each month between January and March for delivery to Fotco, c-and-f basis.
Pakistan also bought one 40,000-tonne cargo of the same fuel oil grade per month for delivery to Keamari.
It bought two 25,000-tonne cargoes of 125-centistoke, 1.0-percent sulphur fuel oil, with each cargo to be delivered in February and March.
The official said the fuel oil prices could not yet be revealed.
